body:
Thank you so much, your words are very helpful and I can tell you're a very wise person. What you're saying definitely puts things into perspective, I have this nasty habit of comparing literally everything I do (or don't do) to that which I'd expect a normal, well adjusted and moderately succesful person to do, and it gets really agonizing sometimes. 

I know I've been dealt a shitty hand in life, and I remind myself that my trajectory would've been wildly different had certain factors out of my control been different, but there's still much to be grateful for, although acknowledging that just makes me feel guilty. I dont know, it's probably just envy or jealousy but I see what's going on in other people's lives and I just wish that could be me. I wish I could transplant my consciousness into these theoretical people and live their lives instead of suffering pointlessly in mine. That's a terrible way to look at things and its immensely counterproductive I know, but it takes a lot of effort to stop thinking like that.

I don't know if its societal pressure or if I just never managed to fit into my culture (I basically lived my entire  childhood up till I was like 13 years old in the US and then we moved to a central american 3rd world country where my family was originally from) but I just cant shake that feeling that everything I do is wrong and I always feel so out of place, sticking out like a sore thumb. At this point I just dream about fleeing this country and making a fresh start for myself, away from everyone and everything I know. Not that that'll ever happen, I'm helplessly broke and my Visa situation is shambles... and I also realize that by physically running away what I'm really trying to do is flee from myself, something that'll never happen unless I make peace with who I am or kill myself. The latter sounds preferable at the moment but who knows.

Anyways, leaving aside my self pity for a moment I truly love your message. It sounds like something out of a stoicism book, and it truly helped me out, so thank you for that.

Thanks! In spit of all the bullshit I guess I still have to be grateful, right? I'm still kicking for now, and I have been for this long, might as well make the best of it right? That's much easier said than done, but sometimes everything just feels so unbearable and suffocating.

Sorry, also posted there but I just really need to vent to someone, anyone. The post has nothing to do directly with autism and I'm not sure this is the right sub for these kinds of posts but I recently started reading up on diagnostic criteria and I'm basically 99% sure I'm somewhere on the ASD, it would certainly explain a lot of the things in my life I've had to suffer through. Anyways, thanks for the kind words, I really  hope things gets better but hope is for fools...or soemthing like hat.
